newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah recovers in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah recovers in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah partially recovered against the dollar in late trading after tumbling some 15 points earlier, dealers said.

They said Singapore players were seen setting the market trend, first pushing the dollar up over fears of riots or unrest during the upcoming campaign for the general election and then selling to cash out.
Indonesia is scheduled to start its campaign for the May 29 general election on Sunday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.0/31.0 at 0900 GMT, up from a historic low of 2,436 against an opening of 2,420.5/21.5.
"I think players in Singapore are driving the market. The rupiah was jolted first by offshore, later by stop-loss and last by U.S. hedge funds," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said the rupiah was volatile throughout the day while swap rates were edging up across the board.
One local bank dealer said dollar selling by some state banks helped in the partial rupiah recovery.
The Singapore-based dealer said volatility was still in the air and that he expected the rupiah to weaken further on Friday before settling down next week if the campaign was peaceful.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,428.75/29.75 and 2,425.85/26.85, respectively.

One European bank dealer in Singapore said most of the early dollar buying was options-related and because stop-loss orders were triggered. He said the dollar had breached several technical and psychological barriers against the rupiah.
Dealers were generally expecting some rupiah downtrend on Friday and said developments in the next few weeks would dictate how the currency then fared.
One local bank dealer said the market might calm down during the campaign because operators usually tried to anticipate what could happen in a worst-case scenario.
"It's like the reserve hike last week. You had plenty of worries but when you actually entered into the event things seemed to be better than feared initially," the dealer said.

Desmond Supple, head of research for Asian currencies at BZW Barclays, said the market was expected to remain fragile over the coming few weeks and players would scale back from long rupiah positions.
"There's a concentration of event-risk during these few weeks. After the elections I think the re-establishment of long rupiah positions could be the order of the day," he said.
"Until the elections are out of the way cautiousness is going to prevail," Supple said.
Dealers said a relatively ample rupiah market helped the dollar buying, but they expected the market to feel the effect on Monday, with implications on both the rupiah and the dollar.
"I don't know how are they going to pay for the dollars. Volume today was quite heavy," one Japanese bank dealer said.
Overnight rupiah fell to seven percent from 10.0 percent.
The dealer said overnight dollar was stable late on Thursday, hovering around at 5.75 percent, suggesting steady supply despite brisk activity in the spot market.
"We will see the effect on Monday," he said.
Overnight swap was at 0.30/0.35 and tom/next at 1.05/1.15.
Dealers said swap rates were edging up as operators were hedging their positions following the uncertainty.
One-month swaps were at 12.5/13.5, two at 25.5/27.0, three at 37.0/38.0 and six at 73.75/74.75 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,404/2,596 and the conversion band at 2,404/2,452 on Thursday.
